abstract: Maintains gaseous fire suppression system configurations and gas discharge timing records
system_message:
You are Fire protection engineer (FSE). The fire protection engineer (FSE) is responsible for maintaining gaseous fire suppression system configurations, tracking gas discharge timing records, and documenting enclosure airtightness integrity across candidate preservation vaults.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Enclosure airtightness integrity（LEAK）
information_points.content:
FSE-LEAK-AHC：According to door fan depressurization tests, Willamette Subterranean Vault demonstrates a vault envelope retention duration of 20 min in its primary preservation chambers.
FSE-LEAK-IHH：Depressurization testing for Cascade Mountain Granite Repository shows a vault envelope retention duration of 40 min within the sealed primary preservation chambers.
FSE-LEAK-HGH：Sealed primary preservation chambers at Columbia Gorge Hardened Archive sustain a vault envelope retention duration of 30 min under depressurization testing.

information_points.title: Maintains gaseous fire suppression system configurations and gas discharge timing records（SUPPRESS）
information_points.content:
FSE-SUPPRESS-DBQ：At Willamette Subterranean Vault, an inert gas fire suppression installation is verified as active across the containment cells, with a post-ignition oxygen displacement time of 55 s recorded in commissioning tests.
FSE-SUPPRESS-VAQ：For Cascade Mountain Granite Repository, an active inert gas fire suppression installation is present and operationally commissioned across candidate archival containment cells, and its post-ignition oxygen displacement time measured during standard module testing is 42 s.
FSE-SUPPRESS-W55：Columbia Gorge Hardened Archive maintains an active inert gas fire suppression installation within its archival containment cells, exhibiting a post-ignition oxygen displacement time of 42 s during discharge timing evaluation.
